results.summary: This project implements a 2-bit adder using combinational logic, with inputs IN1 through IN4 and outputs OUT1 through OUT3. An additional inverter connects IN0 to OUT0, which is not part of the adder. Testing involves toggling the inputs and observing the outputs to verify the addition. External hardware such as an LED display is needed to view the results. The design is a simple educational example created in the Wokwi environment.

This circuit is a counter that increments a 7-segment display using Step and Reset buttons. Logic gates drive the display segments based on the counter output. An optional clock source may be connected for automatic counting. The project serves as an introductory exercise in digital logic and display interfacing within the Wokwi environment.

This circuit is a full adder with two 1-bit operand inputs, a carry-in, and outputs for sum and carry-out. The outputs drive two LEDs (red for sum, blue for carry) to display results. Testing involves applying input combinations and observing the LEDs. It is a basic educational schematic created in Wokwi.

This design implements an 8-bit reverse counter using D flip-flops. It has reset and step buttons for manual control, and outputs drive LEDs. A 10 Hz clock source can be used for automatic counting. The project is a straightforward digital design in Wokwi suitable for learning counters and sequential logic.

This design consists of two D flip-flops with D inputs from IN0 and IN2, and Q outputs at OUT0 and OUT2. Documentation is minimal, providing only basic description and test method. External hardware is not specified. It appears to be a simple educational project created in Wokwi.

This design is a 4-bit adder with carry output built from XOR, AND, and OR gates based on a reference schematic. It takes two 4-bit inputs and produces a 4-bit sum and carry. Testing requires switches for input and LEDs for output. It is an educational exercise created in Wokwi.

This is a simple guessing game: if the correct number is guessed, an LED lights up. It uses a single input (IN3) and a single output (OUT0) to drive the LED. Documentation is very sparse, providing only a brief description. It appears to be a beginner project created in Wokwi.

This design converts a binary input to 7-segment display signals using combinational logic. A decimal point output is always active. Testing involves setting each input individually to verify the corresponding digit. External hardware is a 7-segment display. It is a straightforward educational exercise in Wokwi.

This project implements a 3-bit full adder with inputs A (IN0-IN2), B (IN3-IN5), and carry-in (IN6), producing a 3-bit sum and carry-out. Testing uses switches for input and hex 7-segment LEDs for output. The documentation contains a discrepancy in bit assignments but the intended function is clear. It is an educational Wokwi design.

This design implements a 4-bit ripple counter along with a NAND gate and an AND gate. It uses a clock input, four additional inputs, and six outputs. Testing instructions are minimal, suggesting DIP switches and a hex LED. The project is an initial test of a Wokwi implementation for educational purposes.
